title: Data Science
subtitle: A Lumenary CS elective: the practice of turning data into decisions — the workflow, wrangling and exploring data, visualisation, machine learning on tables, experiments in products, models in production, and doing it responsibly.
description: This elective of [Lumenary CS](/en/cs/) teaches data science as it is practised: asking a good question, getting and cleaning the data, exploring it, modelling it, testing ideas with experiments, putting models into production, and communicating honestly what the data can and cannot say. The methods underneath are taught in [Lumenary Statistics](/en/statistics/); this course puts them to work, and links there rather than re-deriving them.

It assumes Lumenary CS's Start and Core levels and its [learning from data](/en/cs/learning-from-data/) lesson, and the Foundations of Lumenary Statistics. Code is in Python with pandas, NumPy and scikit-learn, and every block with a **Run in browser** button runs there, with nothing to install.

It is written to inform, not to sell: tools and companies are named fairly and by link, and the lessons are as plain about costs, failures and trade-offs as about what works. Every lesson was drafted with AI assistance and is awaiting review by a human expert. The text, exercises and code are original and licensed CC BY-SA 4.0 (code Apache-2.0). Papers, specifications and projects' own documentation are linked, not retold.
